Configure your server

Logs and monitoring

Collect logs, errors, traces and product analytics, and alert on security events and host problems.

Logging

Backend services write structured logs to stdout. LOG_LEVEL is debug, info, warn, error, or off (default info). Production defaults to LOG_FORMAT=json; development defaults to pretty unless you set json or pretty.

Axiom is optional. Set both AXIOM_TOKEN and AXIOM_DATASET for ingest to one shared dataset. Services set service.name (rakazo-api, rakazo-worker, rakazo-sandbox-supervisor, rakazo-updater). A partial Axiom config logs a one-time warning and stays off. AXIOM_EDGE is a regional hostname; AXIOM_EDGE_URL must be https and wins when both are set.

Computer usage events

Computer usage is recorded at several boundaries:

  • run.computer: one record per execution attempt, including runs that never request a computer (reason=none). reason is tool, takeover, or script otherwise; tool is an allowlisted built-in name and trigger identifies user, routine, or other run sources. Deduplicate run.id when counting runs, because a run can have several attempts.
  • computer.requested: the first computer use in an attempt, with its reason, tool, and trigger.
  • computer.provisioned: completed setup, with operation=create, resume, or reuse and durationMs. A setup request can reuse an already-running computer without spending a start.
  • sandbox.start: Boat’s actual create, resume, and recover requests, including starts during preparation or after the provider expires a computer. outcome=accepted means the provider accepted the request, not that all later setup succeeded. rate_limited and failed are separate outcomes. Count accepted creates/resumes for start usage; recoveries are shown separately because their quota treatment depends on the provider.
  • computer.suspended: successful idle or active-limit suspension, with the active duration.

These records use fixed metadata, opaque correlation IDs, durations, and booleans. They do not add prompts, responses, filenames, file contents, command arguments, or credentials. Request/job trace fields link non-run starts back to the API route or background job that initiated them. Axiom is an additional sink for the same logs; these events need no extra keys when ingest is configured.

For example, substitute your own dataset in these APL queries:

['YOUR_DATASET']
| where message == 'sandbox.start'
| summarize requests=count() by provider, operation, outcome
['YOUR_DATASET']
| where message == 'computer.requested'
| summarize requests=count() by trigger, reason, tool
['YOUR_DATASET']
| where message == 'run.computer'
| summarize attempts=count(), withoutComputer=countif(reason == 'none') by trigger

Track accepted starts per hour/day, rate-limit refusals, first-use tools, and the proportion of attempts needing no computer before tuning SANDBOX_IDLE_MS. Increasing the idle window reduces resumes between nearby uses but increases billed runtime; changing it does not remove unnecessary starts caused by tools. Provider rolling-window limits remain the source of truth for quota.

Error reporting

Error reporting to Sentry or a Sentry-compatible collector such as GlitchTip is optional:

  • SENTRY_DSN reports backend error logs, with the exception chain, service, and request or job ids as tags. Uncaught exceptions are reported before exit.
  • SENTRY_BROWSER_DSN reports web app errors. The browser reads it from /api/monitoring/config at startup and posts reports to /api/monitoring/tunnel; the API forwards only envelopes addressed to that DSN. Use a separate project from SENTRY_DSN.
  • SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT names the deployment. SENTRY_RELEASE defaults to the image’s GIT_SHA.

Desktop and mobile use the connected server’s SENTRY_BROWSER_DSN. Electron sends crash metadata without memory dumps. Mobile native reporting requires a rebuilt app; Expo Go is unsupported. For readable mobile crash stacks, build with SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, SENTRY_ORG, SENTRY_PROJECT, and optional SENTRY_URL to upload symbols.

Neither SDK sends cookies, headers, request bodies, user identity, console output, or log context. When ANALYTICS_PSEUDONYM_SECRET is set, reports carry a keyed hash of the signed-in user’s id so the collector can count affected users; the raw id, email and IP address are never sent, and the browser receives its hash from the API. Reporting is off without a DSN; an invalid DSN logs a warning and stays off.

Compose passes these into the API, worker, supervisor, and updater. Computer containers and updater child commands do not receive them.

Tracing

Set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT on the worker to enable optional OpenTelemetry traces (for example, http://otel-collector:4318). The OTLP/HTTP exporter appends /v1/traces to the base endpoint and honors standard OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS (comma-separated key=value pairs) and OTEL_SERVICE_NAME (default rakazo-worker). Compose workers read these settings from .env. With an empty or unset endpoint, no tracing SDK loads or initializes. No collector or hosted service is required to run WhatEverFi.

Traces contain a rakazo.agent.run span with pi.ai.request model-call spans and pi.agent.tool steps, including duration, token usage, cost when known, and success/error status. Each span carries rakazo.bot.id, rakazo.run.id, and rakazo.routine.id when the run belongs to a routine. Helper model calls inherit the same correlation. Pi 0.87.1 exposes built-in telemetry through its newer harness; WhatEverFi’s legacy Agent adapter maps its model and tool lifecycle through the same Pi telemetry contract.

Prompt, response, tool arguments and tool results are excluded by default. OTEL_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true includes them: enable only with a trusted collector and appropriate retention/access controls, since this content can contain secrets or personal data. Unknown attributes and exception messages/stacks stay excluded. Export is batched, best effort, and flushed when the worker shuts down; collector failures do not fail runs.

The standard OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_HEADERS are also passed through, for a collector that takes traces at a different address.

Product analytics

Product analytics is off by default. To enable the PostHog adapter, set ANALYTICS_PROVIDER=posthog, ANALYTICS_KEY to a project capture token, and ANALYTICS_HOST to the HTTPS ingestion host (default https://us.i.posthog.com) on API and worker. Also set ANALYTICS_PSEUDONYM_SECRET to a server-only random value (openssl rand -hex 32), identical on API and worker. Retain it when rotating the public capture token so user and event identities stay stable. Never send this secret to the browser or collector. Set ANALYTICS_PROVIDER=none to disable it. The public website uses its separate PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY configuration.

The backend sends account creation, session creation, fixed screen names, message counts, and run starts/outcomes. Run events include the shared trigger enum; analytics does not read or classify error text. User identifiers are pseudonymized with the server-only secret. No names, emails, prompts, responses, message text, DOM, URLs, search parameters, document contents, request metadata, or raw errors are exported. There is no browser or mobile analytics SDK, autocapture, session replay, or third-party script. Web, Electron, and mobile send only fixed screen/surface enums to the authenticated API; lifecycle events come from the shared backend. This works across clients without giving a collector access to their content. Local and self-hosted installations remain off until their backend is configured.

Delivery is best effort: memory is bounded, requests time out, and shutdown flushes pending events. Analytics failure does not fail product operations. This is not a durable audit trail, and events from before enablement are not backfilled.

Security events

The API and worker append a row to security_events and write a security.event log line for:

  • sign-up, sign-in, sign-out, and failed sign-in or sign-up
  • session revocation, password and passkey changes, and account deletion
  • accounts the identity provider deactivated or reactivated (SCIM)
  • model, MCP, connector, voice, memory, and secret credentials created, changed, or removed
  • deployment settings changes, approval decisions, and approval policy changes
  • refused private or internal destinations (egress.refused) and auth rate-limit hits

Each event has the user, space, client address, user agent, time, and a few identifiers. Events never include message content, secrets, or tokens. Rows older than SECURITY_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS (default 90) are deleted, and Postgres rejects updates to the rows that remain. An account’s own events are also written to its organization’s audit log.

Operators read recent events through server-side database/log tooling. For example, query Postgres:

docker compose --env-file .env -f infra/compose/docker-compose.prod.yml exec postgres \
  psql -U rakazo -d rakazo -c 'SELECT "createdAt", type, ip, "userId", "userAgent", metadata
  FROM security_events ORDER BY "createdAt" DESC LIMIT 50'

Caddy writes a JSON access-log line for each request to stdout. The lines exclude Authorization, Cookie, and Set-Cookie, and URL tokens are replaced with REDACTED. Docker rotates container logs and drops them when it recreates a container. To keep Caddy’s lines, ship container stdout to your log sink with a collector. Security events reach the sink through the API’s own log shipping, and Postgres keeps them too.

What to alert on

The queries below are pseudo-SQL over the JSON log lines, so translate them to your log sink. Field names are the literal keys in each line: message, security.event.type, client.ip, user_agent.original, user.id, and the security.event.metadata object. Tune the thresholds to your traffic.

Sign-up bursts from one address:

SELECT "client.ip", count(*) FROM logs
WHERE message = 'security.event' AND "security.event.type" = 'auth.sign_up'
GROUP BY "client.ip", bucket(1 hour) HAVING count(*) > 3

Password guessing, from one address and across many:

SELECT "client.ip", count(*) FROM logs
WHERE "security.event.type" IN ('auth.sign_in.failed', 'rate_limit.hit')
GROUP BY "client.ip", bucket(15 minutes) HAVING count(*) > 10;

SELECT count(DISTINCT "client.ip") FROM logs
WHERE "security.event.type" = 'auth.sign_in.failed'
GROUP BY bucket(15 minutes) HAVING count(*) > 50

Probes of internal addresses. Any hit deserves a look:

SELECT "user.id", "security.event.metadata.host", "security.event.metadata.reason", count(*)
FROM logs WHERE "security.event.type" = 'egress.refused'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3

Scripted clients on account routes:

SELECT "client.ip", "user_agent.original", count(*) FROM logs
WHERE "security.event.type" LIKE 'auth.%'
  AND ("user_agent.original" IS NULL
    OR lower("user_agent.original") SIMILAR TO '%(curl|wget|python|go-http-client|headless|okhttp|java/)%')
GROUP BY 1, 2

Credential and settings changes from an address that user has not signed in from:

SELECT * FROM logs c
WHERE (c."security.event.type" LIKE 'credential.%'
    OR c."security.event.type" = 'deployment.settings.changed')
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM logs s WHERE s."security.event.type" = 'auth.sign_in'
    AND s."user.id" = c."user.id" AND s."client.ip" = c."client.ip")

Host checks and alerts

Monitoring is opt-in. Install host-alert.py as /usr/local/sbin/rakazo-host-alert and check-host.sh as /usr/local/sbin/rakazo-host-check, and check-services.py as /usr/local/sbin/rakazo-check-services (all executable), then install the supplied host-check service and timer and enable rakazo-host-check.timer. Checks run every five minutes and report low disk space, failed backups, a verified backup older than 36 hours, missing configured IPv4 SSH rules, or installed updates waiting for a reboot. To also check API and worker containers, set RAKAZO_MONITOR_COMPOSE_PROJECT in backup.env to the Compose project name (rakazo-prod for production). The worker probe checks heartbeat and reconciliation freshness. Leave the variable unset if container monitoring is managed elsewhere.

The dedicated-volume check is enabled only by RAKAZO_BACKUP_REQUIRE_VOLUME=1 in backup.env. Identical alerts are suppressed for a day; recovery sends a separate notification.

Alerts go to the system journal by default; no external service is required. For optional Slack delivery, create a root-only /etc/rakazo/alerts.json containing {"slack_webhook":"https://hooks.slack.com/services/REPLACE/ME/SECRET"}. Never commit this file. To notify immediately on backup failure, also install rakazo-backup-alert.service and copy infra/systemd/rakazo-backup-alerts.conf.example to /etc/systemd/system/rakazo-backup.service.d/alerts.conf. Run systemctl daemon-reload after installing units or drop-ins. The base backup service does not require the monitoring tools.

Host audit trail

harden-host.sh installs audit rules for writes to SSH keys, sudoers, accounts, /etc/rakazo, the deployment’s .env, /usr/local/sbin, systemd units, cron, and the Docker daemon config. A rule whose directory does not exist yet, such as the .env before the first clone, is skipped with a notice; rerun the script once it exists. Anyone with root can wipe local logs, so the record only helps once it has left the host.

To ship it, create a root-only /etc/rakazo/audit-ship.env and put the sink’s token in /etc/rakazo/audit-ship.token, then rerun harden-host.sh. Only then does it install audit-ship.py as /usr/local/sbin/rakazo-audit-ship and enable rakazo-audit-ship.service. The sink is any HTTPS endpoint that accepts a JSON array of events with a bearer token, for example Axiom’s https://api.axiom.co/v1/datasets/<dataset>/ingest.

RAKAZO_AUDIT_SINK_URL=https://ingest.example.com/v1/events
# Optional: name the SSH keys you expect (fingerprints from `ssh-keygen -lf key.pub`).
RAKAZO_AUDIT_KNOWN_KEYS=SHA256:replace-with-fingerprint=laptop SHA256:replace-with-fingerprint=ci
# Optional: RAKAZO_AUDIT_TOKEN_FILE (default /etc/rakazo/audit-ship.token), RAKAZO_AUDIT_HOST
# (default: the hostname), and RAKAZO_AUDIT_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS (default 10800, three hours).

Use a token that can only write to that one destination, so a compromised host cannot read or delete what it already sent. The shipper follows /var/log/auth.log and the audit log and sends ssh.login (with key_name, unknown for keys not listed), ssh.failed, sudo.command, su, identity.change, and file.change (with the rule’s watch key and the changed paths), plus a shipper.heartbeat on start and every RAKAZO_AUDIT_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS. Every event carries event, host, source, message, and _time. Offsets advance only after the sink accepts a batch, and failures retry with backoff, so events arrive at least once. On first start it ships the current auth log and starts the audit log at its end. With monitoring installed, the host check alerts when a sink is configured but the shipper is not running.

Alert in the destination, not on the host. Starting points, written as Axiom APL here but plain filters in any log store:

Alert Query
Login with an unnamed key where event == "ssh.login" and key_name == "unknown"
Watched file changed where event == "file.change" outside your own deploys and maintenance
Root use outside the deploy account where (event == "sudo.command" and user != "deploy") or event == "su" or event == "identity.change"
Shipping stopped no shipper.heartbeat from a host for more than two heartbeat intervals
